insights:
- Northeast United FC won 1‑0 with only 45 % possession and 9 shots, yet the goal came from a high‑quality chance (xG 0.36) that materialised – showing xG tells you about the quality of chances, not the final score.
- Mohun Bagan SG held 55 % possession and fired 25 shots, but their higher expected‑goals total (1.48 vs 0.76) did not translate into a goal, illustrating that many of those shots were low‑quality chances.
- The home team had 245 accurate passes to the visitors’ 301, a tighter passing game for them, yet the visitors still completed more passes overall (384 vs 315), indicating a more active but less efficient passing approach.
- Jithin Madathil Subran’s lone goal had an xG of 0.36, meaning roughly one in every three chances he faced turned into a goal—an example of a single high‑quality chance making a decisive difference.
